Three papers report lithium leaching from nickel-containing NMC cathodes into a liquid. 

The first paper is from "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries". The liquid is water. 

The second paper is from "Valuation of Surface Coatings in High-Energy Density Lithium-ion Battery Cathode Materials". The liquid is not specified in the main text. 

The third paper is from "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries". The liquid is not specified in the main text.

prompt.system: You answer questions using only the documents below: pages selected from them, with tables written row by row. Answer briefly. If you compute a number, show the calculation. If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so.

expect: ethylene glycol (cssc-2020): Li content 1.015 to 0.993 (p5.L65-68); Cyrene (susmat-2020): ether groups attract lithium, numbers only in Table S1, not in the text (p5.L19-26); water (ensm-2020): NMC 811 leached ~3 wt% Li after one week (p5.L62-63)
